events.excerpt: This is Ethlabs’ view on post-quantum and post-AI timelines and how we think Ethereum’s protocol layer should prioritize them, after spending a week with coredevs at Devcon. tl;dr We think Ethereum can become post-quantum and (plausibly) post-AI in 2027: pqai27. This will future-proof Ethereum’s leading position as the credible decentralized root of trust for the global economy, with ETH as the programmable store of value at its center. Being post-quantum is not enough, we intend on being post-AI too. AI capabilities are taking off: quantum timelines are moving forward, AI is solving open maths problems that pose the question whether some cryptographic primitives might break, and it’s finding software vulnerabilities at scale. Ethereum is uniquely positioned for this moment and leading the way : years of prior research and work have produced a clear plan to become post-quantum and plausibly post-AI, and now we should make it the priority. The network is resilient through its decentralized validator set and client diversity, and formal verification is already deeply embedded into its core development process. pqai27 means rethinking upcoming hardforks , including Hegotá: anything not on the critical path to pqai should be reconsidered. events.excerpt: A group of privacy enthusiasts discovered on Tuesday that the default software development kit (SDK) that wallet apps use to connect to Ledger hardware devices transmits details regarding crypto transaction signatures to Ledger servers. When the discovery spread on social media, privacy proponents were surprised to discover that Ledger crypto wallet apps have been quietly broadcasting transaction details to Ledger. The behavior has been a default since Ledger’s context-module version 1.16, i.e. since May 2026 or earlier. It was a devastating discovery for users who have mistakenly thought the default behavior of Ledger wallets was private signing and private broadcasts of transactions directly to blockchain networks. Unfortunately, many Ledger wallets have been simultaneously doxxing personal details to the world’s largest hardware wallet manufacturer. Substantial metadata has been transmitting from Ledger devices to Ledger servers since late May. Apps and users must opt-out of this information-sharing behavior when using wallet apps, and the overwhelming majority do not. Ambire developer Kaloyan Kosev (also known as “superKalo”) flagged the issue yesterday: Ledger servers have been receiving customers’ Ledger model, software version, as well as blockchain address users paid or q

events.excerpt: ERC-3668 (CCIP-Read) lets a contract hand a read off to a gateway, but the gateway either has to be trusted or has to return a proof the contract can verify. For many cross-chain reads a valid proof cannot be produced. That does not make the read unsafe, because the client usually already trusts its own RPC connection to the other chain and could simply make the call itself. ERC-8446 lets the client act as the gateway. The contract reverts with OffchainLookup as usual, with an x-chain URL that names the chain and contract to read, and the client calls that contract with its own RPC and passes the result to the callback exactly as eth_call returns it. No third party is involved. The chain and address are encoded as an ERC-7930 Interoperable Address, for example USDC on Base. x-chain:0x0001000002210514833589fcd6edb6e08f4c7c32d4f71b54bda02913 An optional ?finalized=true makes the read at the finalized block instead of the latest one. The client alone decides whether it can safely read a given chain, and never takes RPC endpoints from the contract. Nested x-chain lookups are not followed, so each call makes at most one cross-chain hop. Contracts can also tell when a client does not support the ERC. They add a data: URL after the x-chain URL, which only older clients reach, and it del
events.headline: ERC-8446: Cross-Chain Client Gateway for CCIP-Read

events.excerpt: ERC-8048 and ERC-8049 store metadata onchain as key-value pairs, but a JSON document has no compact way to point at those values. A URL that names the contract, the chain, and the token ID repeats what the client already knows and differs for every token. ERC-8493 defines the onchain URI scheme. The contract and token ID are not written in the URI, they come from the function that returned the document. { "image": "onchain:image/png", "thumbnail": { "small": "onchain:image/png?key=thumb.small" } } onchain:image/png is 17 bytes and works unchanged for every token. When the URI comes from tokenURI or uri , the client reads it with metadata(tokenId, key) from ERC-8048, and when it comes from contractURI , with metadata(key) from ERC-8049. A direct member of the top-level document uses its own name as the key, and everywhere else the key parameter names it. Tokens that are already deployed can use the scheme by adding a metadata_contract property to their JSON, which points the client at a separate metadata contract. Linked JSON documents keep the same contract and token, so the whole thing reads as one data tree. The scheme adds no contract surface. Existing ERC-8048 and ERC-8049 contracts support it with no change, and a client that does not know the scheme sees a URI it can ignore
events.headline: ERC-8493: Onchain URI Scheme

events.excerpt: Summary LlamaRisk is building Aave’s Risk Layer: automated risk solutions that make expert risk judgment verifiable, with every parameter, bound and action checkable onchain. The Aave Risk Framework set this direction in June by making continuous risk oracles part of the protocol’s standing infrastructure. Governance and manual review can trail a fast-moving event by hours, and the evolution of AI capabilities keeps shortening the time between finding a weakness and exploiting it, so protection has to run continuously and at machine speed. LlamaGuard PT went live in September as the first of these solutions. We continue the rollout with LlamaGuard Caps as the next addition. Aave’s greatest strength is its liquidity, deep enough to move capital instantly and at scale. Defending access to that liquidity programmatically protects Aave’s users, even when a failure elsewhere in DeFi puts compromised collateral or stolen assets in play. LlamaGuard Caps hardens Aave’s perimeter. Its first stage, a borrow rate limiter for Aave V3, gives each reserve a margin of borrowing room above its debt, sized to the reserve. events.excerpt: XRP co-creator and former Ripple CTO David “Joel Katz” Schwartz says he hasn’t “bought XRP in a long time” and that holding Ripple stock is riskier than he’d like. Posting to X on Monday, Schwartz said his aversion to risk has led him to sell “nearly all of the digital assets I’ve ever held.” Schwartz also revealed that he sold around 2.5 million XRP in 2025 while paying $1.7 million in capital gains tax on the sale. I haven't bought XRP in a long time. I am very uncomfortable with risk and have sold nearly all of the digital assets I've ever held. I still hold quite a bit of Ripple stock, and that alone is more risk than I wish I had. — David 'JoelKatz' Schwartz (@JoelKatz) November 9, 2026 Many XRP fans took Schwartz’s statement as a sign he doesn’t like XRP. Read more: Ripple-linked Uphold faces withdrawal delays amid ‘bank run’ claims According to Schwartz, he received this XRP in 2020 and 2023 when it hit highs of $0.6 and of $0.8 respectively. It then surged to $3.65 in 2025, increases of 508% and 356%. According to Nasdaq Private Market, a secondary market stock tracker, Ripple shares are worth almost $94, down 22% over the last year but up 237% across the last two years. events.excerpt: This is a Testnet release. It is not suggested for Mainnet use. Alpenglow is now the only available consensus mode. The following configuration keys are no longer supported: [consensus] alpenglow , [tiles.tower] write_vote_history_file , and [tiles.txsend] txsend_src_port Added a new failover mechanism between two Firedancer validators, designed to be easy to use, fast, and secure. Refer to the failover guide for details Support for all Solana 4.4 features Support for geo_aware_leader_schedule ( SIMD-0675 ), validator_location_registration ( SIMD-0674 ), and stricter_shred_validation ( SIMD-0504 ) features Reduced mainnet memory usage from 159 to 142 GiB The transaction cache and cost tracker gained fallback disk paths, which will not be written during routine or healthy operations. Configurable at [paths] txncache and [paths] cost_tracker Added a new iavf kernel-bypass networking provider for Intel ice/i40e NICs through SR-IOV virtual functions Added an experimental auction scheduling strategy for block packing, enabled with [tiles.pack] schedule_strategy = "auction" Improvements to the experimental efficient mode ( [layout] mode = "efficient" )
